page: Microsoft Azure FX96-24ms_v2 is a specialized instance configuration that pairs high single-core compute performance with an exceptionally large memory allocation. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the virtual machine provides 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores using the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. Supported hardware capabilities include a 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix acceleration flags such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance incorporates 1832.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a resource ratio of 76.33 GB of memory per vCPU.

Benchmark evaluations show prominent single-thread throughput, with the instance scoring 2366.0 on the Geekbench single-core benchmark and placing in the top ten percent. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 34.65 GB/sec, while single-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 14.37 GB/sec, reflecting top-quartile performance. In multi-core tests, the server registered a Geekbench multi-core score of 16770.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 41641.31. Memory operations demonstrated strong uncached large-block write bandwidth at 118.92 GB/sec, while small-block cached read throughput registered 2070.15 GB/sec.

The primary operational tradeoff of the FX96-24ms_v2 involves its asymmetric architecture. While providing nearly two terabytes of memory, total core parallelism is constrained to 24 vCPUs, and the instance includes no local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, requiring external premium network storage for persistent disk access. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile is tailored to reduce software licensing costs that scale by CPU core count while maintaining immense in-memory data capacity. Suitable workloads comprise large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), memory-constrained analytics pipelines, and caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure FX96-24ms_v2 is a memory-dense compute instance engineered for workloads demanding high memory capacity per core and elevated clock speeds. Powered by a 12-core, 24-vCPU Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the system integrates 1832.0 GB of memory alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. It lacks local ephemeral disk storage and hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage. Benchmark results place its single-core compute performance in the top ten percent, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2366.0 and strong uncached large-block memory write bandwidth of 118.92 GB/sec. This configuration offers distinct qualitative efficiency for applications governed by per-core software licensing that still require substantial RAM. The FX96-24ms_v2 is particularly suited for massive in-memory databases, electronic design automation, real-time analytics, and caching tiers.
